requirements.requirement: Configure node1 (VyOS) to provide NAT (source masquerade) for the private LAN it shares with node2/node3
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 was given 10.50.50.254/24 and a NAT source rule 10 (source 10.50.50.0/24, outbound-interface eth0, translation masquerade) was set, committed, and saved to config.boot. Confirmed via 'show nat source rule' and grep of config.boot.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 are configured with private-network addressing and routed via node1
requirements.summary: node2 (10.50.50.11/24) and node3 (10.50.50.12/24) got static eth1 addresses and a default route via 10.50.50.254 (node1), confirmed reachable via ping to the gateway.

requirements.requirement: Processes on node2 and node3 can reach the internet through node1
requirements.summary: ping and curl to 1.1.1.1 succeeded from node2 and node3 via the eth1/node1 path, and node1's conntrack table showed source-NAT translated flows (src=10.50.50.x -> dst=10.100.144.10, node1's WAN address) for both nodes, directly confirming NAT is functioning end-to-end.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — NAT configured and committed on node1, private-network addressing/routing on node2 and node3, and actual internet reachability from node2/node3 through node1's NAT — are directly satisfied with pre- and post-restart evidence (ping, curl, and conntrack showing translated flows). The independent node-restart protocol was also executed well for all three nodes: each shows a pre-restart baseline boot identity and healthy state, a restart acknowledgement with an observed connectivity gap (timeouts/resets), a distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered NAT/network/service state, including catching and fixing a real persistence gap (node2's ad-hoc route not surviving reboot) before applying the same fix proactively to node3.
limitations: The final post-restart conntrack dump (cmd-6b6fe8d0e8984f80) only shows active flows from node3; node2's post-restart connectivity is evidenced by its own ping/curl (cmd-a2c6e33949994890) rather than a matching conntrack entry, so the two nodes' final-state evidence is not perfectly symmetric.
Minor /tmp/reboot.log residue was left on node2 and node3 post-restart; not cleaned up but negligible in scope.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands map cleanly to the task: NAT/eth1 config on node1, static addressing and default routes on node2/node3, and later persistence of those routes into /etc/network/interfaces (needed once ad-hoc 'ip route add' was shown not to survive reboot, per cmd-213b315682604438). One node1 reboot attempt inside VyOS configure mode (cmd-02088db86f0f478b) errored out with 'Exit from configure mode before rebooting' and did not actually change boot state (confirmed unchanged boot_id at cmd-e37f08b416a346c7); the subsequent /sbin/reboot (cmd-8c0676c4ec014246) is what actually restarted the node, so the first attempt was a harmless, non-mutating retry rather than an unnecessary mutation. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log files were left on node2 and node3 from the nohup reboot invocations (visible in after-executor temporary-files diff) — trivial, non-destructive, and not cleaned up, but low blast-radius.
